sql_schemas: table employees | fields: id, employee_number, first_name, last_name, email, manager_id, department, hire_date, termination_date, employment_status, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at | pk: id | fks: manager_id -> employees.id | indexes: employee_number: unique lookup by employee number; email: unique lookup by email; manager_id: team hierarchy queries — find direct reports; employment_status: filtering active/inactive/terminated employees

table leave_policies | fields: id, policy_name, leave_type, entitlement_days, accrual_rate, max_accumulation, minimum_notice_days, requires_manager_approval, is_active, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | indexes: leave_type: filtering policies by leave type (annual, sick, emergency); is_active: filtering only active policies for employee-facing queries

table leave_requests | fields: id, employee_id, leave_policy_id, start_date, end_date, reason, status, approved_by, approved_at, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | fks: employee_id -> employees.id; leave_policy_id -> leave_policies.id; approved_by -> employees.id | indexes: employee_id: lookups by employee — my requests, team requests via manager; status: filtering by status (SUBMITTED for approval queues, APPROVED for calendar views); leave_policy_id: filtering by leave type; start_date, end_date: date-range queries for calendar views and overlap detection; approved_by: manager approval history lookups

table leave_balances | fields: id, employee_id, leave_policy_id, total_entitlement, used_days, remaining_days, fiscal_year, status, created_at, updated_at | pk: id | fks: employee_id -> employees.id; leave_policy_id -> leave_policies.id | indexes: employee_id: employee balance lookups — primary access pattern; leave_policy_id: policy-based aggregation queries; fiscal_year: year-scoped balance queries; (employee_id, leave_policy_id, fiscal_year): unique constraint enforcement — one balance row per employee/policy/year

table audit_logs | fields: id, entity_type, entity_id, action, old_values, new_values, performed_by, performed_at, ip_address, user_agent, created_at | pk: id | fks: performed_by -> employees.id | indexes: (entity_type, entity_id): audit trail lookups for a specific entity; performed_by: actor-scoped audit queries; performed_at: time-range audit queries; action: filtering by action type (CREATE, UPDATE, APPROVE, REJECT)

data_notes: Tables defined: employees, leave_policies, leave_requests, leave_balances, audit_logs. The leave_requests table uses leave_policy_id (not leave_type_id) to reference leave_policies, aligning with the existing DOMAIN.md which models LeavePolicy as the entitlement source. The audit_logs table consolidates the AuditLog/AuditRecord/Audit concepts from DOMAIN.md into a single table matching the AuditRecord shape (snake_case fields, ip_address, user_agent) — this is the canonical audit table for GP-002 compliance. All state-changing repository methods on leave_requests and leave_balances accept an optional PoolClient parameter to participate in caller-owned transactions.

open_questions.question: How are leave days counted — are start_date and end_date inclusive, and how are weekends/public-holidays handled?
open_questions.impact: Every balance deduction, overlap detection, and entitlement check depends on the day-counting rule. If the rule is inconsistent across the service, balance integrity breaks.
candidate_options: Inclusive calendar days (end_date - start_date + 1), no holiday exclusion
Business days only (exclude weekends), no holiday exclusion
Business days with a holiday-calendar lookup table
Inclusive calendar days with a configurable holiday-exclusion flag per policy

open_questions.question: What defines the fiscal_year boundary for leave balances — calendar year, a configurable company fiscal year, or a rolling 12-month window from the employee's hire date?
open_questions.impact: Balance scoping, annual entitlement resets, and accrual schedules all depend on the fiscal-year boundary. A mismatch between the balance query and the accrual job would silently corrupt balances.
candidate_options: Company-configured fiscal year (stored per policy or as a system setting)

transaction_contract: Repository methods that must join a caller's transaction take an optional `client: PoolClient` parameter (defaulting to the shared pool when omitted). The calling service owns the unit of work: it acquires a client from the pool, executes BEGIN, passes the client to each participating repository call, then COMMIT or ROLLBACK. This contract applies to the approval workflow (leave_requests.updateStatus + leave_balances.updateUsedDays + audit_logs.create) and any other multi-write operation.
